Cyclist magazine issue 180: on sale now

Cyclist magazine Issue 180, November 2026, is on sale now. Subscribe to Cyclist or buy issue 180 here.

Wherever you go on Tenerife, Mount Teide is impossible to ignore. At 3,718m this volcanic peak is not just the highest mountain on this or any of the Canary Islands, it’s the tallest in all of Spain. Its volcanic nature also lends its slopes a dramatic visual aspect, with barren slopes and field of black basalt boulders giving the whole place an alien feel.

Teide’s otherworldly nature, the challenge of conquering its slopes and the Canaries’ consistently good weather make this an excellent place to ride a bike, which is exactly why we decided to pay it a visit for our Big Ride in the November 2026 issue of Cyclist magazine, available now on newsstands and from the Cyclist Store.

The volcano itself is far from the only thing Tenerife has to offer visitors on two wheels, however. Great food, superb views and ever-evolving riding conditions thanks to the island’s many microclimates mean there’s never a dull moment on any ride here, as we discovered on our 135km loop.

Fast forward a few months and we reckon you’ll have good odds of seeing Netcompany Ineos sprinter Dorian Godon on the slopes of Mount Teide on an early-season training camp with his team. But if that’s too long to wait, you can spot him in the pages of our November issue as we pay a visit to the fast-finishing Frenchman’s home in Girona to spend a day with the man himself. And from his banana-juggling exercise routines to his grocery runs on a vintage steel bike, it’s safe to say the moustachioed Godon is far from your ordinary pro rider.

Cannondale’s CAAD, meanwhile, is far from your ordinary road bike. Championing the merits of aluminium in an era increasingly dominated by carbon, the CAAD has stood apart among modern high-end performance platforms from day one, and has the Grand Tour wins to prove it. That makes it a worthy subject for the latest instalment of our Bike History series, and this issue we chart the bike’s heritage over more than four decades, from its spiritual forebear the ST500 right up to 2026’s cutting edge CAAD 14.

How hard can any three-minute bike ride really be? Pretty damn hard, as it happens – at least when the three minutes in question are the Catford Hill Climb. This annual celebration of suffering lays claim to being the world’s oldest continuously held bike race, and this year we decided to embrace its glorious madness ourselves by lining up on the start line. We’re still not entirely sure it was a good idea.

Also in the November 2026 issue of Cyclist, we join half a million other fans on the slopes of Alpe d’Huez during the Tour de France to get a taste of what is surely cycling’s biggest party, visit its mercifully far quieter French neighbour the Col du Grand Colombier, showcase the best hydration packs on the market and find out what happened to graphene, the wonder-material that at one point was seen as the next big thing in cycling.

On the reviews front, we test out a pair of high-performance road bikes in the Wilier Rapida and Kuota K-A1 as well as BMC’s second-generation Kaius gravel race bike, alongside reviews of the Specialized S-Works Evade 4 helmet and Oquo’s RA57Ltd wheelset. There’s plenty more besides in the latest issue of Cyclist, so make sure to pick up your copy on newsstands or at the Cyclist Store or get a Cyclist magazine subscription to have every issue delivered free, straight to your door.
